title.zh: 卷437 列傳二百二十四 荣禄 王文韶 张之洞 瞿鸿禨
title.en: Volume 437 Biographies 224: Rong Lu, Wang Wenshao, Zhang Zhidong, Qu Hongji
title.raw: 卷437 列傳二百二十四 荣禄 王文韶 张之洞 瞿鸿禨

sentences.zh: 榮祿，字仲華，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Rong Lu, courtesy name Zhonghua, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu, whose courtesy name was Zhonghua, belonged to the Guwalgiya clan and came from the Manchu Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 祖喀什噶爾幫辦大臣塔斯哈，父總兵長壽，均見忠義傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tasgha, assistant commissioner at Kashgar, and his father Changshou, a regional commander, are both recorded in the Loyal and Righteous biographies.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tasgha, who served as assistant commissioner at Kashgar, and his father Changshou, a regional commander, both appear in the biographies of the loyal and righteous.

sentences.zh: 榮祿以廕生賞主事，隸工部，晉員外郎。

translations.literal: Rong Lu entered office through hereditary privilege as a principal clerk in the Board of Works and was promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege Rong Lu received appointment as a principal clerk in the Board of Works and rose to vice director.

sentences.zh: 出為直隸候補道。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as an expectant intendant in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was then posted as an expectant intendant in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 同治初，設神機營，賞五品京堂，充翼長，兼專操大臣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tongzhi reign the Shenji Camp was established; he was granted fifth-rank Beijing service and served as wing commander, concurrently as specialist drill commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi reign, when the Shenji firearms camp was established, he was granted fifth-rank Beijing service, appointed wing commander, and made concurrent specialist drill commissioner.

sentences.zh: 再遷左翼總兵。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to commander of the Left Wing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to commander of the Left Wing.

sentences.zh: 用大學士文祥薦，改工部侍郎，調戶部，兼總管內務府大臣。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Grand Secretary Wen Xiang he was transferred to vice minister of the Board of Works, then to the Board of Revenue, and concurrently made superintendent of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: On Grand Secretary Wen Xiang's recommendation he was moved to vice minister of Works, then to Revenue, and concurrently appointed superintendent of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 穆宗崩，德宗嗣統。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong died, Emperor Dezong succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Muzong's death, Emperor Dezong ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 榮祿言於恭親王，乃請頒詔，俟嗣皇帝有子，承繼穆宗。

translations.literal: Rong Lu spoke to Prince Gong, and they then requested an edict that when the heir emperor had a son, that son should succeed Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu urged Prince Gong to seek an edict providing that when the heir emperor should have a son, that son would succeed Emperor Muzong.

sentences.zh: 其後始定以紹統者為嗣。

translations.literal: Only afterward was it finally fixed that the successor-by-adoption would be heir.
translations.idiomatic: Only later was it settled that the adopted successor would stand as heir.

sentences.zh: ，兼步軍統領。

translations.literal: , and concurrently served as commander of the Metropolitan Infantry Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: , and he was also appointed commander of the Metropolitan Infantry Brigade.

sentences.zh: 遷左都御史，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief and promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Left Censor-in-Chief and then promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 慈禧皇太后嘗欲自選宮監，榮祿奏非祖制，忤旨。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Cixi once wished to choose eunuchs herself; Rong Lu memorialized that this was not ancestral practice and offended her.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Cixi once sought to select palace eunuchs herself, Rong Lu protested that this violated ancestral practice and drew her displeasure.

sentences.zh: 會學士寶廷奏言滿大臣兼差多，乃解尚書及內務府差。

translations.literal: When Academician Bao Ting memorialized that Manchu grand ministers held too many concurrent posts, he was relieved of the ministries of Works and the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: When Academician Bao Ting reported that Manchu grand ministers held too many concurrent posts, Rong Lu was stripped of his posts as Minister of Works and superintendent of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 又以被劾納賄，降二級，旋開復，出為西安將軍。

translations.literal: He was also impeached for taking bribes, demoted two ranks, soon restored, and sent out as military governor of Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: After further impeachment for bribery he was demoted two ranks, soon restored, and appointed military governor of Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 二十年，祝嘏留京，再授步軍統領。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he remained in the capital for birthday felicitations and was again appointed commander of the Metropolitan Infantry Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Guangxu he stayed in the capital for imperial birthday celebrations and was again made commander of the Metropolitan Infantry Brigade.

sentences.zh: 日本構釁，恭親王、慶親王督辦軍務，榮祿參其事。

translations.literal: When Japan provoked hostilities, Prince Gong and Prince Qing supervised military affairs, and Rong Lu took part.
translations.idiomatic: When Japan opened hostilities, Prince Gong and Prince Qing directed military affairs with Rong Lu among their staff.

sentences.zh: 和議成，疏薦溫處道袁世凱練新軍，是曰「新建陸軍」。

translations.literal: After peace was made he memorialized recommending Yuan Shikai, intendant at Wenzhou, to drill a new army—this was the so-called "Newly Established Army."
translations.idiomatic: After peace he recommended Yuan Shikai, then intendant at Wenzhou, to train a new army—the force later known as the Newly Established Army.

sentences.zh: 授兵部尚書、協辦大學士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of War and associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of War and associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 疏請益練新軍，而調甘肅提督董福祥軍入衛京師。

translations.literal: He memorialized to expand training of the new army and to transfer Gansu regional commander Dong Fuxiang's troops to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He urged further expansion of the new army and the transfer of Gansu regional commander Dong Fuxiang's force to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，晉大學士，命為直隸總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was promoted to grand secretary and appointed governor-general of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he became grand secretary and governor-general of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 是時上擢用主事康有為及知府譚嗣同等參預新政，議變法，斥舊臣，召直隸按察使袁世凱入覲，超授侍郎，統練兵。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor promoted Clerk Kang Youwei and Prefect Tan Sitong and others to take part in the new policies, debated reform, dismissed old ministers, summoned Zhili judicial commissioner Yuan Shikai to audience, and abruptly appointed him vice minister to command troop training.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then elevated Clerk Kang Youwei, Prefect Tan Sitong, and others into the new-policy councils, debated sweeping reform, sidelined veteran ministers, summoned Zhili judicial commissioner Yuan Shikai for audience, and abruptly made him vice minister in charge of military training.

sentences.zh: 榮祿不自安，御史楊崇伊奏請太后再垂簾，於是太后复臨朝訓政，召榮祿為軍機大臣，以世凱代之，命查拿康有為，斬譚嗣同等六人於市，以上有疾，詔徵醫；

translations.literal: Rong Lu felt insecure; Censor Yang Chongyi memorialized asking the empress dowager to resume the curtain; thereupon the empress dowager again held court behind the curtain, summoned Rong Lu as grand councillor, replaced him with Yuan Shikai, ordered Kang Youwei seized, and executed Tan Sitong and five others in the market; citing the emperor's illness, an edict summoned physicians.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy, Rong Lu watched as Censor Yang Chongyi asked the empress dowager to resume regency; she did, recalled Rong Lu to the Grand Council, put Yuan Shikai in his Zhili post, ordered Kang Youwei arrested, and had Tan Sitong and five others executed in the marketplace while an edict, citing the emperor's illness, called for physicians.

sentences.zh: 復命榮祿管兵部，仍節制北洋海陸各軍。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to manage the Board of War while still commanding all Beiyang land and sea forces.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu was again placed over the Board of War while retaining command of all Beiyang land and sea forces.

sentences.zh: 榮祿乃奏設武衛軍，以聶士成駐蘆臺為前軍，董福祥駐薊州為後軍，宋慶駐山海關為左軍，世凱駐小站為右軍，而自募萬人為中軍，駐南苑。

translations.literal: Rong Lu then memorialized to establish the Wuwei Army: Nie Shicheng at Lutai as Front Army, Dong Fuxiang at Jizhou as Rear Army, Song Qing at Shanhaiguan as Left Army, Yuan Shikai at Xiaozhan as Right Army, and he himself raised ten thousand men as Central Army at the Southern Hunting Park.
translations.idiomatic: He then organized the Wuwei Army—Nie Shicheng at Lutai as the Front Army, Dong Fuxiang at Jizhou as the Rear, Song Qing at Shanhaiguan as the Left, Yuan Shikai at Xiaozhan as the Right, and ten thousand men he raised himself as the Central Army at the Southern Hunting Park.

sentences.zh: 時太后議廢帝，立端王載漪子溥俊為穆宗嗣，患外人為梗，用榮祿言，改稱「大阿哥」。

translations.literal: At that time the empress dowager planned to depose the emperor and install Prince Duan's son Pujun as Muzong's heir; fearing foreign obstruction, on Rong Lu's advice the title was changed to "Great Heir Apparent."
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager planned to depose Guangxu and install Prince Duan's son Pujun as heir to Muzong, fearing foreign interference she followed Rong Lu's counsel and styled the boy merely "Great Heir Apparent."

sentences.zh: 二十六年，拳匪亂作，載漪等稱其術，太后信之，欲倚以排外人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer disturbance broke out; Zaiyi and others praised their arts, the empress dowager believed them, and wished to rely on them to drive out foreigners.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer uprising began; Zaiyi and others extolled Boxer magic, the empress dowager trusted them, and hoped to use them against foreigners.

sentences.zh: 福祥率甘軍攻使館，月餘不下；

translations.literal: Fuxiang led the Gansu army to attack the legations but for more than a month could not take them.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Fuxiang led the Gansu troops against the legation quarter yet failed to reduce it for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 榮祿不能阻，載漪等益橫，京師大亂，駢戮忠諫大臣。

translations.literal: Rong Lu could not stop them; Zaiyi and others grew more overbearing, the capital fell into great disorder, and loyal remonstrating ministers were slaughtered in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu could not restrain them; Zaiyi and his faction grew bolder, the capital descended into chaos, and ministers who spoke loyal truth were cut down one after another.

sentences.zh: 榮祿踉蹌入言，太后厲色斥之。

translations.literal: Rong Lu stumbled in to remonstrate, and the empress dowager rebuked him sternly.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong Lu staggered in to plead, the empress dowager glared and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 聯軍入京，兩宮西幸，駐蹕太原。

translations.literal: The allied armies entered the capital; the two sovereigns fled west and halted at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Allied forces entered Beijing; the two courts fled west and lodged at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 榮祿請赴行在，不許，命為留京辦事大臣。

translations.literal: Rong Lu requested to join the traveling court but was not permitted and was ordered to remain in the capital as resident minister.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu asked to join the flight but was refused and left in Beijing as resident minister.

sentences.zh: 已而詔詣西安，既至，寵禮有加，賞黃馬褂，賜雙眼花翎、紫韁。

translations.literal: Soon an edict summoned him to Xi'an; on arrival favor was heaped on him—he was granted the yellow jacket, double-eyed peacock feather, and purple reins.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to Xi'an, where extraordinary honors followed: the yellow jacket, double-eyed peacock feather, and purple reins.

sentences.zh: 隨扈還京，加太子太保，轉文華殿大學士。

translations.literal: He escorted them back to the capital, was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and transferred to Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Escorting the court home, he received Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and became Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 二十九年卒，贈太傅，諡文忠，晉一等男爵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor, given the posthumous title Wenzhong, and promoted to first-class baron.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-ninth year, was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor with the temple name Wenzhong, and advanced to first-class baron.

sentences.zh: 榮祿久直內廷，得太后信仗。

translations.literal: Rong Lu had long served within the palace and enjoyed the empress dowager's trust.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu had long served inside the palace and held the empress dowager's confidence.

sentences.zh: 眷顧之隆，一時無比。

translations.literal: The favor shown him was unmatched in his day.
translations.idiomatic: No official of his time received such favor.

sentences.zh: 事無鉅細，常待一言決焉。

translations.literal: Whether the matter was great or small, it often awaited a word from him to be decided.
translations.idiomatic: Great or small, affairs often waited on his word alone.

sentences.zh: 王文韶，字夔石，浙江仁和人。

translations.literal: Wang Wenshao, courtesy name Kuishi, was a native of Renhe in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenshao, courtesy name Kuishi, came from Renhe in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年進士，銓戶部主事。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the second year of Xianfeng, he was selected as principal clerk in the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Xianfeng, he was appointed principal clerk in the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中，出為湖北安襄鄖荊道。

translations.literal: He was promoted through director to intendant of Anxiang, Xiangyang, and Jingzhou in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through director to intendant over Anxiang, Xiangyang, and Jingzhou in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠、李鴻章皆薦其才。

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang and Li Hongzhang both recommended his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Both Zuo Zongtang and Li Hongzhang commended his ability.

sentences.zh: 擢按察使，遷湖南布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to judicial commissioner and then to financial commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He became judicial commissioner and then financial commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 同治十年，署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tongzhi he served as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tongzhi he acted as governor.

sentences.zh: 黔苗亂熾，桂東淪寇域。

translations.literal: Miao rebellions in Guizhou raged fiercely and eastern Guangxi fell into bandit territory.
translations.idiomatic: Miao uprisings in Guizhou burned hot while eastern Guangxi slipped under rebel control.

sentences.zh: 文韶條上援黔、防境機宜，以兵事屬按察使席寶田，督其部將蘇元春、龔繼昌等進剿，斬首逆張秀眉烏鴉坡，黔境平。

translations.literal: Wenshao submitted detailed plans for aiding Guizhou and defending the border; he placed military affairs under judicial commissioner Xi Baotian, who with subordinate generals Su Yuanchun, Gong Jichang, and others advanced, beheading the rebel leader Zhang Xiumei at Wuyapo, and Guizhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshao laid out plans to aid Guizhou and secure the frontier, entrusted operations to Judicial Commissioner Xi Baotian, and through generals Su Yuanchun and Gong Jichang beheaded the rebel Zhang Xiumei at Wuyapo, pacifying Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 文韶繪苗疆要塞圖，上之朝。

translations.literal: Wenshao drew a map of Miao frontier strongholds and presented it to court.
translations.idiomatic: He mapped the Miao frontier fortresses and sent the chart to court.

sentences.zh: 十一年，除真。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he received regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he received full appointment as governor.

sentences.zh: 寧遠莠民倡亂，耒陽硃鴻英复妄稱明裔構眾，先後檄道員陳寶箴討平之。

translations.literal: Villainous people at Ningyuan stirred trouble, and Zhu Hongying at Leiyang falsely claimed Ming descent to raise crowds; he successively ordered Intendant Chen Baozhen to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Bad elements at Ningyuan rose in revolt and Zhu Hongying at Leiyang pretended Ming descent to gather mobs; Wenshao repeatedly ordered Intendant Chen Baozhen to crush them.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，遣總兵謝晉鈞平新化、衡、永土寇。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he dispatched Regional Commander Xie Jinjun to pacify bandits in Xinhua, Hengzhou, and Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu's first year he sent Regional Commander Xie Jinjun to quell brigands in Xinhua, Hengzhou, and Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 撫湘六年，內治稱靜謐焉。

translations.literal: For six years as Hunan governor his internal administration was praised as tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: During six years governing Hunan his civil administration won praise for calm order.

sentences.zh: 入權兵部侍郎，直軍機。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as acting vice minister of War and served on the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as acting vice minister of War and joined the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 會歲旱，各省籥災，中旨罪己。

translations.literal: When drought struck several provinces and memorials reported disaster, an imperial rescript blamed the throne.
translations.idiomatic: As drought spread and provinces reported famine, the throne issued a self-reproach edict.

sentences.zh: 文韶亦自陳無狀，詔革職留任。

translations.literal: Wenshao also confessed his own failures, and an edict removed him from office while retaining him in post.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshao confessed his shortcomings and was ordered dismissed yet kept at his duties.

sentences.zh: 旋除禮部侍郎，兼總理衙門行走。

translations.literal: Soon he was made vice minister of Rites and concurrently served in the Zongli Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice minister of Rites and given concurrent service in the Zongli Yamen.

sentences.zh: 八年，御史洪良品、鄧承修劾雲南軍需案，文韶坐失察，奪二級。

translations.literal: In the eighth year censors Hong Liangpin and Deng Chengxiu impeached the Yunnan military supplies case; Wenshao was punished for lack of supervision and stripped of two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Censors Hong Liangpin and Deng Chengxiu attacked the Yunnan military-supplies scandal; Wenshao lost two ranks for inadequate oversight.

sentences.zh: 乞養歸，終母喪，還前除。

translations.literal: He requested leave to nurse his mother, completed mourning, and was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He sought leave to care for his mother, completed mourning, and returned to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he became governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 武定會匪陷富民、祿勸，人心恟懼。

translations.literal: Society-bandits at Wuding seized Fumin and Luquan, and popular panic spread.
translations.idiomatic: When secret-society rebels at Wuding took Fumin and Luquan, fear swept the region.

sentences.zh: 文韶斬獲叛將，三日而定。

translations.literal: Wenshao beheaded the captured rebel leaders and order was restored in three days.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshao executed the rebel chiefs and restored order within three days.

sentences.zh: 無何，鎮邊夷亂起，檄迤南道劉春霖分道進攻，拓地三百里。

translations.literal: Before long border tribes in Zhenbian rose; he ordered Southern Circuit Commissioner Liu Chunlin to attack on separate routes and extended territory three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Border tribes in Zhenbian soon rebelled; he sent Commissioner Liu Chunlin on divided columns, extending control three hundred li.

sentences.zh: 徙建廳城於猛朗，募勇屯墾。

translations.literal: He moved the prefectural seat to Menglang and recruited militia for garrison farming.
translations.idiomatic: He relocated the prefectural seat to Menglang and recruited militia for garrison farming.

sentences.zh: 改臨安猛丁歸流，移府經歷駐其地。

translations.literal: He converted Mengding in Lin'an from native to regular administration and posted a prefectural aide there.
translations.idiomatic: He brought Mengding in Lin'an under regular administration and stationed a prefectural aide on site.

sentences.zh: 其餘寇亂及土族叛服不常，皆隨時殄滅。

translations.literal: Other bandit disturbances and tribal defection and submission were suppressed as they arose.
translations.idiomatic: Other raids and shifting tribal loyalties he crushed whenever they appeared.

sentences.zh: 初，英、法並緬、越後，西南緣邊防務益棘。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Britain and France absorbed Burma and Annam, southwestern frontier defense grew more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: After Britain and France absorbed Burma and Annam, defense along the southwestern frontier grew acute.

sentences.zh: 文韶綏靖各路土司，令自為守。

translations.literal: Wenshao pacified the various native chieftains and ordered them to guard themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshao soothed the native chieftains and left them to defend their own domains.

sentences.zh: 會日韓啟釁，詔入都詢方略。

translations.literal: When Japan and Korea opened hostilities an edict summoned him to the capital to discuss strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out between Japan and Korea, he was summoned to the capital for strategy.

sentences.zh: 既至，奉幫辦北洋之命。

translations.literal: On arrival he received orders to assist in Beiyang affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Beijing he was ordered to assist Beiyang affairs.

sentences.zh: 鴻章赴日議和，文韶權直隸總督、北洋大臣。

translations.literal: When Hongzhang went to Japan to negotiate peace, Wenshao acted as governor-general of Zhili and Beiyang minister.
translations.idiomatic: While Li Hongzhang negotiated in Japan, Wenshao acted as Zhili governor-general and Beiyang minister.

sentences.zh: 和議成，實授。

translations.literal: After peace was concluded he received regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After peace he received full appointment.

sentences.zh: 時關內外主客軍四百餘營，酌留湘、淮、豫三十營，餘悉散遣，士卒帖然。

translations.literal: At that time within and beyond the passes more than four hundred camps of guest and home troops stood; he retained thirty Hunan, Huai, and Henan camps and dispersed the rest, and the soldiers accepted it calmly.
translations.idiomatic: More than four hundred guest and home camps then garrisoned north China; he kept thirty Hunan, Huai, and Henan battalions, disbanded the rest, and the troops accepted the change without unrest.

sentences.zh: 建議籌修旅大砲台，謂：「旅順舊台密於防前，疏於防後，敵自大連灣入，遂失所芘；

translations.literal: He proposed rebuilding the Lüda batteries, saying: "The old Lüshun forts were dense before the enemy and sparse behind; when the enemy entered from Dalian Bay shelter was lost.
translations.idiomatic: He urged rebuilding the Lüda fortifications, arguing that old Lüshun batteries were thick toward the sea but thin to the rear, so an enemy entering Dalian Bay left the port undefended.

sentences.zh: 大連舊台，專顧防海，未及防陸，敵自金州登岸，遂不能支。

translations.literal: The old Dalian forts looked only to sea defense and not land defense; when the enemy landed at Jinzhou they could not hold.
translations.idiomatic: Dalian's old works guarded the sea alone; when the enemy landed at Jinzhou they collapsed.

sentences.zh: 今重整海防，必彌其罅隙。

translations.literal: Now in reorganizing coastal defense the gaps must be closed.
translations.idiomatic: Rebuilding coastal defense, he said, required closing every gap.

sentences.zh: 」又請加意水師、武備各學堂，以儲將才，嫺武幹，俟財力稍足，徐圖擴充。

translations.literal: " He also asked special attention for naval and military academies to store command talent and train martial administrators, to expand gradually when finances allowed.
translations.idiomatic: He also pressed for stronger naval and military academies to train officers and staff, to be enlarged as funds permitted.

sentences.zh: 又陳河運漕糧積弊，請蘇漕統歸海運，他若勘吉林三姓金礦、磁州煤礦，踵鴻章後次第成之，而京漢鐵路亦興築於是時矣。

translations.literal: He also reported accumulated abuses in grain transport by the Grand Canal and asked that Suzhou grain tax be unified under sea transport; surveying gold mines in Jilin's Three Surnames and coal at Cizhou followed Li Hongzhang's lead and were completed in turn, and the Beijing-Hankou railway was also begun at this time.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed Grand Canal transport abuses and urged shifting Suzhou grain to sea carriage; gold mines in Jilin's Three Surnames and Cizhou coal, following Li Hongzhang's initiatives, came on line in turn, and the Beijing-Hankou railway was launched in these years.

sentences.zh: 又奏設北洋大學堂、鐵路學堂、育才館、俄文館，造就甚眾。

translations.literal: He also memorialized founding the Beiyang University, railway school, talent cultivation hall, and Russian language school, producing many graduates.
translations.idiomatic: He founded Beiyang University, a railway school, a talent hall, and a Russian language school, training a large cohort of students.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，入贊軍機，以戶部尚書協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he entered the Grand Council as Minister of Revenue and associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he joined the Grand Council as Minister of Revenue and associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，拳匪仇教，文韶力言外釁不可啟，不見納。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxers hated Christianity; Wenshao strongly urged that foreign trouble must not be provoked, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, as Boxers turned on Christians, Wenshao warned repeatedly against provoking foreign powers and was ignored.

sentences.zh: 宮車既出，三日，始追及懷來。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage had already departed; only after three days did he catch up at Huailai.
translations.idiomatic: The court had already fled; three days passed before he overtook it at Huailai.

sentences.zh: 自聯軍犯京，事急，兩宮召軍機，惟文韶一人入見，諭必侍行。

translations.literal: From the allied attack on the capital, when affairs grew urgent the two sovereigns summoned the Grand Council but only Wenshao was admitted to audience and told he must accompany them.
translations.idiomatic: When allies threatened Beijing and the court summoned the Grand Council in crisis, only Wenshao was admitted and told he must travel with them.

sentences.zh: 至是立召對，泣慰之，遂隨扈，自晉入秦，晉體仁閣大學士。

translations.literal: He was then immediately called to audience; they wept and comforted him, and he escorted them from Shanxi into Shaanxi and was made Grand Secretary of the Tiren Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Called at once to audience, the sovereigns wept and comforted him; he escorted them from Shanxi into Shaanxi and was made Grand Secretary of the Tiren Hall.

sentences.zh: 明年，改外務部會辦大臣，旋賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: The next year he was made co-minister of foreign affairs and soon granted the yellow jacket.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became co-minister of foreign affairs and soon received the yellow jacket.

sentences.zh: 署全權大臣，命先還京，佐辦中俄條約。

translations.literal: As plenipotentiary he was ordered to return to the capital first to assist in the Sino-Russian treaty.
translations.idiomatic: Made plenipotentiary, he was sent back to Beijing ahead of the court to help negotiate the Sino-Russian treaty.

sentences.zh: 交還東三省及關外鐵路，事寧，賞雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: After the return of the three eastern provinces and railways beyond the pass, when affairs were settled he was granted double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When the three eastern provinces and railways beyond the pass were restored and matters settled, he received the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 充政務處大臣，督辦路礦總局。

translations.literal: He served as minister on the Political Affairs Council and supervised the Railway and Mining Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He sat on the Political Affairs Council and directed the Railway and Mining Bureau.

sentences.zh: 轉文淵閣，晉武英殿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Wenyuan Pavilion and promoted to the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He moved from the Wenyuan Pavilion to Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，免直軍機。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was removed from the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he left the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 明年，稱疾乞休。

translations.literal: The next year he pleaded illness and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he cited illness and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 文韶歷官中外，詳練吏職，究識大體，然更事久，明於趨避，亦往往被口語。

translations.literal: Wenshao served at court and in the provinces, was skilled in administrative detail and grasped the larger pattern, yet long experience made him adept at self-preservation and he was often criticized in private talk.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshao served widely, mastered routine administration and broad policy, yet decades in office taught him caution and gossip often called him too prudent.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，鄉舉重逢，賜太子太保。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he again met the provincial examination cycle of his jinshi year and was granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he celebrated the jinshi cycle of his year and received Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 其冬，卒，年七十九，晉贈太保，諡文勤。

translations.literal: That winter he died at seventy-nine; he was posthumously promoted to Grand Guardian with the posthumous title Wenqin.
translations.idiomatic: He died that winter at seventy-nine, posthumously honored as Grand Guardian with the temple name Wenqin.

sentences.zh: 張之洞，字香濤，直隸南皮人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhidong, courtesy name Xiangtao, was a native of Nanpi in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhidong, courtesy name Xiangtao, came from Nanpi in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 少有大略，務博覽為詞章，記誦絕人。

translations.literal: In youth he had great breadth of vision, made wide reading and belles-lettres his task, and his memory was unmatched among men.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he thought on a grand scale, devoured books and polished prose, and possessed a memory few could match.

sentences.zh: 年十六，舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: At sixteen he took first place in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he ranked first in the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，成進士，廷對策不循常式，用一甲三名授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he became jinshi; his palace examination answer did not follow convention, and he was appointed compiler in the third place of the first class.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi's second year he passed the jinshi; his palace examination essay broke convention and he was named compiler as third of the first class.

sentences.zh: 六年，充浙江鄉試副考官，旋督湖北學政。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he served as associate examiner for the Zhejiang provincial examination, then was made educational commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he assisted the Zhejiang provincial exams, then became Hubei educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十二年，典試四川，就授學政。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he served as chief examiner for Sichuan and was appointed educational commissioner on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he chief-examined Sichuan and was appointed educational commissioner there.

sentences.zh: 所取士多俊才，遊其門者，皆私自喜得為學塗徑。

translations.literal: The scholars he selected were mostly outstanding talent; those who studied under him privately rejoiced to have found a path in learning.
translations.idiomatic: Most scholars he chose were brilliant men, and those who entered his circle privately rejoiced to have found a true path in learning.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，擢司業，再遷洗馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu he was promoted to vice director of education and then to groom of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangxu he rose to vice director of education and then groom of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 之洞以文儒致清要，遇事敢為大言。

translations.literal: Zhidong, as a literary Confucian, attained eminent court posts and when affairs arose dared to speak boldly.
translations.idiomatic: A literary scholar who rose to eminent posts, Zhidong spoke boldly whenever affairs demanded.

sentences.zh: 俄人議歸伊犁，與使俄大臣崇厚訂新約十八條。

translations.literal: When Russia discussed returning Yili, Minister to Russia Chonghou concluded a new treaty of eighteen articles.
translations.idiomatic: When Russia negotiated the return of Yili, Minister to Russia Chonghou signed a new eighteen-article treaty.

sentences.zh: 之洞論奏其失，請斬崇厚，毀俄約。

translations.literal: Zhidong memorialized on its errors, asking that Chonghou be beheaded and the Russian treaty destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong attacked the treaty in memorials, demanded Chonghou's execution, and urged abrogation of the Russian agreement.

sentences.zh: 疏上，乃褫崇厚職治罪，以侍郎曾紀澤為使俄大臣，議改約。

translations.literal: When the memorial went up, Chonghou was stripped of office and punished; Vice Minister Zeng Jize was made minister to Russia to negotiate revision.
translations.idiomatic: The throne stripped and punished Chonghou and sent Vice Minister Zeng Jize to Russia to renegotiate.

sentences.zh: 六年，授侍講，再遷庶子。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed expositor and twice promoted to sublector.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became court expositor and soon rose to sublector of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 复論紀澤定約執成見，但論界務，不爭商務，並附陳設防、練兵之策。

translations.literal: He again criticized Zeng Jize for fixing the treaty with set opinions, disputing only boundaries and not commercial rights, and appended plans for defense and troop training.
translations.idiomatic: He again faulted Zeng Jize for clinging to preconceptions—haggling over borders while yielding commercial rights—and appended proposals for frontier defense and military training.

sentences.zh: 疏凡七八上。

translations.literal: His memorials totaled seven or eight.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted seven or eight such memorials in all.

sentences.zh: 往者詞臣率雍容養望，自之洞喜言事，同時寶廷、陳寶琛、張佩綸輩崛起，糾彈時政，號為清流。

translations.literal: Formerly literary officials mostly cultivated reputation at ease; from Zhidong's delight in speaking on affairs, Bao Ting, Chen Baochen, Zhang Peilun, and others rose together, impeaching current policy, and were called the Pure Stream.
translations.idiomatic: Literary officials had usually cultivated reputation in comfort; Zhidong's appetite for policy debate helped Bao Ting, Chen Baochen, Zhang Peilun, and others rise as the "Pure Stream," impeaching the times.

sentences.zh: 七年，由侍講學士擢閣學。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted from expositor of the Hanlin Academy to Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he rose from Hanlin expositor to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 俄授山西巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed governor of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 當大祲後，首劾布政使葆亨、冀寧道王定安等黷貨，舉廉明吏五人，條上治晉要務，未及行，移督兩廣。

translations.literal: After great famine he first impeached Financial Commissioner Baoheng, Jining Circuit Intendant Wang Ding'an, and others for corruption, recommended five upright officials, and listed essentials for governing Shanxi; before they could be carried out he was transferred to supervise the two Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: After severe famine he impeached corrupt officials including Commissioner Baoheng and Intendant Wang Ding'an, named five upright men, and outlined essentials of Shanxi governance—then was transferred to the two Guang before his program took effect.

sentences.zh: 八年，法越事起，建議當速遣師赴援，示以戰意，乃可居間調解。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Franco-Vietnamese affair arose; he proposed that troops be sent quickly to aid, showing warlike intent so mediation could then be undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: When the Franco-Vietnamese crisis erupted in the eighth year, he urged rapid dispatch of relief forces to show readiness to fight, thereby strengthening China's hand in mediation.

sentences.zh: 因薦唐炯、徐延旭、張曜材任將帥。

translations.literal: He therefore recommended Tang Jiong, Xu Yanxu, and Zhang Yao as fit for command.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Tang Jiong, Xu Yanxu, and Zhang Yao for field command.

sentences.zh: 十年春，入覲。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year he entered audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the tenth year he was called to audience.

sentences.zh: 四月，兩廣總督張樹聲解任專治軍，遂以之洞代。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Governor-General Zhang Shusheng was relieved to devote himself to military affairs, and Zhidong replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Zhang Shusheng stepped down to focus on the war and Zhidong succeeded him as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 當是時，雲貴總督岑毓英、廣西巡撫潘鼎新皆出督師，尚書彭玉麟治兵廣東。

translations.literal: At that time Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Cen Yuying and Guangxi Governor Pan Dingxin both went out to command armies, and Minister Peng Yulin directed troops in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Cen Yuying of Yunnan-Guizhou and Guangxi Governor Pan Dingxin commanded in the field while Minister Peng Yulin directed Guangdong forces.

sentences.zh: 越將劉永福者，故中國人，素驍勇，與法抗。

translations.literal: The Vietnamese general Liu Yongfu was formerly a Chinese subject, always valiant in battle, and resisted the French.
translations.idiomatic: Vietnamese commander Liu Yongfu, originally Chinese and famed for valor, fought the French.

sentences.zh: 法攻越未能下，復分兵攻台灣，其後遂據基隆。

translations.literal: France could not reduce Vietnam and again divided forces to attack Taiwan, afterward occupying Keelung.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to subdue Vietnam, France sent another column against Taiwan and eventually held Keelung.

sentences.zh: 朝議和戰久不決，之洞至，言戰事氣自倍，以玉麟夙著威望，虛己聽從之。

translations.literal: Court debate on war or peace long remained unsettled; when Zhidong arrived his war spirit doubled, and because Yulin enjoyed old prestige he humbly followed Yulin's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: With court opinion deadlocked, Zhidong's arrival doubled fighting spirit; deferring to Peng Yulin's prestige, he followed the elder general's lead.

sentences.zh: 奏請主事唐景崧募健卒出關，與永福相犄角。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking Clerk Tang Jingsong to recruit stalwart troops to cross the border and coordinate with Yongfu in pincer fashion.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Clerk Tang Jingsong recruit tough fighters to cross the border and coordinate with Yongfu in a pincer.

sentences.zh: 朝旨因就加永福提督、景崧五品卿銜，炯、延旭亦皆已至巡撫，當前敵，被劾得罪去，並坐舉者。

translations.literal: The court therefore promoted Yongfu to regional commander and Jingsong to fifth-rank court rank; Jiong and Yanxu had already reached governorships facing the enemy front but were impeached, convicted, and removed, and their recommenders were punished with them.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Yongfu regional commander and gave Jingsong fifth-rank rank; Tang Jiong and Xu Yanxu, already on the front as governors, were impeached, cashiered, and their patrons punished alongside them.

sentences.zh: 之洞獨以籌餉械勞，免議。

translations.literal: Zhidong alone, for labor in raising funds and ordnance, was exempted from censure.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhidong, credited with supplying funds and arms, escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 廣西軍既敗於越，朝旨免鼎新，以提督蘇元春統其軍，而之洞復奏遣提督馮子材、總兵王孝祺等，皆宿將，於是滇、越兩軍合扼鎮南關，殊死戰，遂克諒山。

translations.literal: After Guangxi forces were defeated in Vietnam, the court removed Dingxin and put Regional Commander Su Yuanchun in command; Zhidong again memorialized dispatching Regional Commander Feng Zicai and Regional Commander Wang Xiaoqi and others—all veteran generals—so Yunnan and Guangxi armies united to hold Zhennanguan, fought desperately, and took Lang Son.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangxi troops fell in Vietnam, Pan Dingxin was removed and Su Yuanchun took over; Zhidong sent veterans Feng Zicai and Wang Xiaoqi until Yunnan and Guangxi forces jointly held Zhennanguan, fought to the death, and captured Lang Son.

sentences.zh: 會法提督孤拔攻閩、浙，砲毀其坐船，孤拔殪，而我軍不知，法原停戰，廷議許焉。

translations.literal: Meanwhile French Admiral Courbet attacked Fujian and Zhejiang; cannon destroyed his flagship and Courbet perished, but our army did not know it; France had originally agreed to cease fire, and the court approved.
translations.idiomatic: French Admiral Courbet struck Fujian and Zhejiang; Chinese guns sank his flagship and killed him, but our forces did not know it; France had already agreed to a truce, which the court accepted.

sentences.zh: 授李鴻章全權大臣，定約，以北圻為界。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang was appointed plenipotentiary and fixed the treaty with Tonkin as the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang negotiated the treaty setting the border at Tonkin.

sentences.zh: 敘克諒山功，賞花翎。

translations.literal: For merit in taking Lang Son he was granted peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: For the Lang Son victory he received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 之洞恥言和，則陰自圖強，設廣東水陸師學堂，創槍砲廠，開礦務局。

translations.literal: Zhidong, ashamed to speak of peace, secretly sought self-strengthening, establishing Guangdong naval and army academies, founding an arsenal, and opening a mining bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of mere peace talk, Zhidong quietly pursued self-strengthening—naval and army schools, an arsenal, and a mining bureau in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 疏請大治水師，歲提專款購兵艦。

translations.literal: He memorialized to build up the navy greatly, with annual special funds to purchase warships.
translations.idiomatic: He urged a major naval buildup funded by annual appropriations for warships.

sentences.zh: 復立廣雅書院。

translations.literal: He also founded the Guangya Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He also established the Guangya Academy.

sentences.zh: 武備文事並舉。

translations.literal: Military preparedness and literary culture were pursued together.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued arms and letters together.

sentences.zh: 十二年，兼署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he concurrently served as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he acted concurrently as governor.

sentences.zh: 於兩粵邊防控制之宜，輒多更置。

translations.literal: On measures proper for controlling the two Guang frontiers he often made many changes.
translations.idiomatic: He frequently reorganized the two Guang frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 著沿海險要圖說上之。

translations.literal: He compiled an illustrated account of coastal danger points and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He drew up an illustrated coastal defense manual and sent it to court.

sentences.zh: 在粵六年，調補兩湖。

translations.literal: After six years in Guang he was transferred to the two Hu.
translations.idiomatic: After six years in Guangdong he was moved to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 會海軍衙門奏請修京通鐵路，臺諫爭陳鐵路之害，請停辦。

translations.literal: When the Naval Yamen memorialized to build the Beijing-Tongzhou railway, censors repeatedly cited railway harms and asked that work stop.
translations.idiomatic: When the Naval Yamen proposed the Beijing-Tongzhou railway, censors protested the dangers of railways and demanded a halt.

sentences.zh: 翁同龢等請試修邊地，便用兵；

translations.literal: Weng Tonghe and others asked trial construction on the frontier for military convenience;
translations.idiomatic: Weng Tonghe and others urged trial lines on the frontier for military use;

sentences.zh: 徐會灃請改修德州濟寧路，利漕運。

translations.literal: Xu Huifeng asked instead the Dezhou-Jining route to benefit grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huifeng favored a Dezhou-Jining line to aid Grand Canal transport.

sentences.zh: 之洞議曰：「修路之利，以通土貨、厚民生為最大，徵兵、轉餉次之。

translations.literal: Zhidong argued: "The greatest benefit of building railways is moving native goods and enriching people's livelihood; troop movement and grain transport come second.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong argued: "Railways chiefly move native goods and enrich livelihoods; troop movement and grain transport rank second.

sentences.zh: 今宜自京外盧溝橋起，經河南以達湖北漢口鎮。

translations.literal: Now it should run from Lugou Bridge outside the capital through Henan to Hankou in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: The trunk line should run from Lugou Bridge outside Beijing through Henan to Hankou in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 此幹路樞紐，中國大利所萃也。

translations.literal: This trunk hub is where China's greatest profits gather.
translations.idiomatic: That trunk would become the hub where China's greatest economic gains converged.

sentences.zh: 河北路成，則三晉之轍接於井陘，關隴之驂交於洛口；

translations.literal: When the Hebei section was finished, Shanxi carts would reach Jingxing and Shaanxi teams would meet at Luokou;
translations.idiomatic: Once the Hebei segment opened, Shanxi traffic would reach Jingxing and Shaanxi convoys would meet at Luokou;

sentences.zh: 自河以南，則東引淮、吳，南通湘、蜀，萬里聲息，刻期可通。

translations.literal: south of the river it would draw Huai and Wu eastward and Hunan and Shu southward, so news could cross ten thousand li in set time.
translations.idiomatic: south of the Yellow River it would link Huai and Wu to the east and Hunan and Sichuan to the south, carrying news across ten thousand li on schedule.

sentences.zh: 其便利有數端：內處腹地，無慮引敵，利一；

translations.literal: Its conveniences were several: lying in the interior, no fear of luring the enemy—benefit one;
translations.idiomatic: He listed seven benefits: an interior route would not invite invasion;

sentences.zh: 原野廣漠，墳廬易避，利二；

translations.literal: broad wilderness, graves easily avoided—benefit two;
translations.idiomatic: open country would spare graves;

sentences.zh: 廠盛站多，役夫賈客可舍舊圖新，利三；

translations.literal: many factories and stations, laborers and merchants could shift from old to new—benefit three;
translations.idiomatic: numerous stations would let laborers and merchants adapt;

sentences.zh: 以一路控八九省之衢，人貨輻輳，足裕餉源，利四；

translations.literal: one road controlling thoroughfares of eight or nine provinces, people and goods converging, ample revenue—benefit four;
translations.idiomatic: one line would command eight or nine provinces and swell revenue;

sentences.zh: 近畿有事，淮、楚精兵崇朝可集，利五；

translations.literal: if trouble arose near the capital, Huai and Chu elite troops could assemble within a morning—benefit five;
translations.idiomatic: trouble near the capital could summon Huai and Chu veterans within a morning;

sentences.zh: 太原旺煤鐵，運行便則開採必多，利六；

translations.literal: Taiyuan's rich coal and iron, once transport was easy mining would multiply—benefit six;
translations.idiomatic: cheap transport would expand Taiyuan's coal and iron;

sentences.zh: 海上用兵，漕運無梗，利七。

translations.literal: war at sea would not block grain transport—benefit seven.
translations.idiomatic: war at sea would not choke grain supply.

sentences.zh: 有此七利，分段分年成之。

translations.literal: With these seven benefits, it should be built in sections year by year.
translations.idiomatic: With these seven gains, he urged sectional construction year by year.

sentences.zh: 北路責之直隸總督，南路責之湖廣總督，副以河南巡撫。

translations.literal: The northern section would be the Zhili governor-general's responsibility, the southern the Huguang governor-general's, assisted by the Henan governor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili would build the northern segment, Huguang the southern, with Henan assisting.

sentences.zh: 」得旨報可，遂有移楚之命。

translations.literal: " Approval was received, and thereupon came the order transferring him to Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved, and he was transferred to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 大冶產鐵，江西萍鄉產煤，之洞乃奏開鍊鐵廠漢陽大別山下，資路用，兼設槍砲鋼藥專廠。

translations.literal: Daye produced iron and Pingxiang in Jiangxi produced coal; Zhidong memorialized opening an ironworks below Daye Hill at Hanyang for railway use, and also specialized factories for guns, cannon, and powder.
translations.idiomatic: Daye iron and Jiangxi Pingxiang coal led him to open an ironworks at Hanyang under Daye Hill for the railway, plus specialized gun, cannon, and powder plants.

sentences.zh: 又以荊襄宜桑棉麻枲而饒皮革，設織布、紡紗、繅絲、制麻革諸局，佐之以堤工，通之以幣政。

translations.literal: Because Jingxiang was rich in mulberry, cotton, hemp, and ramie and abundant in leather, he set up weaving, spinning, silk-reeling, and leather works, aided by dike projects and currency reform.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxiang's silk, cotton, hemp, and leather supported weaving, spinning, silk-reeling, and leather factories, backed by dikes and currency reform.

sentences.zh: 由是湖北財賦稱饒，土木工作亦日興矣。

translations.literal: Thereby Hubei revenues grew ample and construction works daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei revenues grew rich and public works multiplied.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，中東事棘，代劉坤一督兩江，至則巡閱江防，購新出後膛砲，改築西式砲台，設專將專兵領之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the Sino-Japanese crisis grew acute; he replaced Liu Kunyi as governor-general of the two Jiang and on arrival inspected river defenses, purchased new breech-loading cannon, rebuilt Western-style batteries, and appointed dedicated generals and troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, as the Sino-Japanese crisis sharpened, he replaced Liu Kunyi in the two Jiang, inspected river defenses, bought breech-loading guns, rebuilt Western batteries, and assigned dedicated commanders.

sentences.zh: 募德人教練，名曰「江南自強軍」。

translations.literal: He recruited Germans to drill them, named the "Jiangnan Self-Strengthening Army."
translations.idiomatic: German instructors trained the "Jiangnan Self-Strengthening Army."

sentences.zh: 採東西規制，廣立武備、農工商、鐵路、方言、軍醫諸學堂。

translations.literal: Adopting East and West models, he broadly founded academies for military affairs, agriculture, industry, commerce, railways, languages, and army medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Following Eastern and Western models, he founded military, agricultural, industrial, commercial, railway, language, and army medical schools.

sentences.zh: 尋還任湖北。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to his Hubei post.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to Hubei.

sentences.zh: 時國威新挫，朝士日議變法，廢時文，改試策論。

translations.literal: At that time national prestige had just suffered setback and court scholars daily debated reform, abolishing the eight-legged essay and changing to policy discourse examinations.
translations.idiomatic: National prestige freshly wounded, court scholars debated reform—abolishing eight-legged essays for policy examinations.

sentences.zh: 之洞言：「廢時文，非廢五經、四書也，故文體必正，命題之意必嚴。

translations.literal: Zhidong said: "Abolishing the essay form is not abolishing the Five Classics and Four Books; therefore essay style must be correct and examination themes must be strict.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong warned: abolishing essay form did not mean abandoning the classics—style and themes must stay rigorous.

sentences.zh: 否則國家重教之旨不顯，必致不讀經文，背道忘本，非細故也。

translations.literal: Otherwise the state's weight on teaching would not appear, inevitably leading to not reading the classics, turning from the Way and forgetting roots—not a small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise students would neglect the classics, abandon the Way, and forget their roots.

sentences.zh: 今宜首場試史論及本朝政法，二場試時務，三場以經義終焉。

translations.literal: Now the first session should test historical discourse and current dynasty law and government, the second current affairs, the third ending in classical exposition.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed first testing history and Qing institutions, second current affairs, third classical exposition.

sentences.zh: 各隨場去留而層遞取之，庶少流弊。

translations.literal: Each session eliminating candidates in layers would reduce abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Elimination after each session would curb abuses.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「武科宜罷騎射、刀石，專試火器。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The military examination should drop mounted archery and stone-lifting and test only firearms.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged ending mounted archery and stone-lifting in military exams in favor of firearms.

sentences.zh: 欲挽重文輕武之習，必使兵皆識字，勵行伍以科舉。

translations.literal: To reverse the habit of valuing letters and slighting arms, soldiers must learn to read and military ranks should be opened to examination success.
translations.idiomatic: To reverse contempt for soldiers, troops must learn literacy and examination honors should reach the ranks.

sentences.zh: 」二十四年，政變作，之洞先著勸學篇以見意，得免議。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-fourth year when the political coup occurred, Zhidong had earlier published Exhortation to Learning to show his stance and escaped censure.
translations.idiomatic: When the 1898 coup came, his earlier Exhortation to Learning showed his stance and spared him blame.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，京師拳亂，時坤一督兩江，鴻章督兩廣，袁世凱撫山東，要請之洞，同與外國領事定保護東南之約。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year when the capital Boxer disturbance arose, Kunyi then governed the two Jiang, Hongzhang the two Guang, and Yuan Shikai governed Shandong; they urgently summoned Zhidong to join foreign consuls in pledging protection of the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: During the 1900 Boxer crisis, Kunyi, Hongzhang, and Yuan Shikai summoned Zhidong to pledge with foreign consuls to protect the southeast.

sentences.zh: 及聯軍內犯，兩宮西幸，而東南幸無事。

translations.literal: When the allied armies invaded inland and the two sovereigns fled west, the southeast fortunately remained undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: When allies invaded and the court fled west, the southeast stayed calm.

sentences.zh: 明年，和議成，兩宮回鑾。

translations.literal: The next year peace was made and the two sovereigns returned.
translations.idiomatic: Peace followed the next year and the court returned.

sentences.zh: 論功，加太子少保。

translations.literal: For merit he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He received Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent for his service.

sentences.zh: 以兵事粗定，乃與坤一合上變法三疏。

translations.literal: As military affairs were roughly settled, he and Kunyi jointly submitted three memorials on reform.
translations.idiomatic: With fighting subsiding, he and Kunyi submitted three reform memorials.

sentences.zh: 其論中國積弱不振之故，宜變通者十二事，宜採西法者十一事。

translations.literal: They discussed twelve causes of China's chronic weakness and eleven Western methods to adopt.
translations.idiomatic: They listed twelve causes of weakness and eleven Western reforms to adopt.

sentences.zh: 於是停捐納，去書吏，考差役，卹刑獄，籌八旗生計，裁屯衛，汰綠營，定礦律、商律、路律、交涉律，行銀圓，取印花稅，擴郵政。

translations.literal: Thereupon purchase of offices stopped, clerks were removed, runners examined, prisons relieved, Eight Banner livelihoods provided for, garrison posts cut, Green Standard troops thinned, mining, commercial, railway, and treaty laws set, silver dollars issued, stamp tax levied, and postal service expanded.
translations.idiomatic: Purchase of office ended, clerks and runners reformed, prisons eased, Banner livelihoods funded, garrisons cut, Green Standards thinned, new commercial and mining laws enacted, silver dollars and stamp tax introduced, and postal service expanded.

sentences.zh: 其尤要者，則設學堂，停科舉，獎遊學。

translations.literal: Most important were establishing schools, stopping examinations, and rewarding study abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Schools, abolition of the old examinations, and rewards for overseas study mattered most.

sentences.zh: 皆次第行焉。

translations.literal: All were carried out in turn.
translations.idiomatic: These reforms rolled out step by step.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，充督辦商務大臣，再署兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he served as superintendent of commerce and again acted as governor-general of the two Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he supervised commerce and again acted in the two Jiang.

sentences.zh: 有道員私獻商人金二十萬為壽，請開礦海州，立劾罷之。

translations.literal: A circuit intendant privately offered a merchant two hundred thousand in birthday cash to open mines at Haizhou; Zhidong impeached and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: When a circuit intendant offered a merchant two hundred thousand taels for birthday favors to open Haizhou mines, Zhidong impeached and removed him.

sentences.zh: 考鹽法利弊，設兵輪緝私，歲有贏課。

translations.literal: He examined salt-law pros and cons, set armed patrol boats against smuggling, and yearly produced surplus revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing salt administration, he deployed armed patrols against smuggling and produced annual surpluses.

sentences.zh: 明年，入覲，充經濟特科閱卷大臣，釐定大學堂章程，畢，仍命還任。

translations.literal: The next year he entered audience, served as examiner for the special economic examination, finalized university regulations, and on completion was ordered back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he entered audience, examined the special economic candidates, finalized university statutes, and returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 陛辭奏對，請化除滿、漢畛域，以彰聖德，遏亂萌，上為動​​容。

translations.literal: At farewell audience he asked to dissolve Manchu-Han barriers to display sagely virtue and check disorder at its root; the emperor was deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: At farewell audience he urged breaking Manchu-Han barriers to display imperial virtue and curb unrest; the throne was moved.

sentences.zh: 旋裁巡撫，以之洞兼之。

translations.literal: Soon the governorship was abolished and Zhidong held it concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiangsu governorship was abolished, Zhidong held it concurrently.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，晉協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was promoted to associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he became associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 未幾，內召，擢體仁閣大學士，授軍機大臣，兼筦學部。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned to the capital, promoted to Grand Secretary of the Tiren Hall, appointed grand councillor, and concurrently directed the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Soon summoned to Beijing, he became Tiren Hall grand secretary, grand councillor, and head of the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，督辦粵漢鐵路。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he supervised the Guang-Han Railway.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he supervised the Guang-Han Railway.

sentences.zh: 德宗暨慈禧皇太后相繼崩，醇親王載灃監國攝政。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong and Empress Dowager Cixi died in succession; Prince Chun Zai Feng served as regent.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxu and Cixi died in succession; Prince Chun Zai Feng became regent.

sentences.zh: 之洞以顧命重臣晉太子太保。

translations.literal: Zhidong as a trusted minister on the deathbed council was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: As a deathbed trusted minister, Zhidong received Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 逾年，親貴浸用事，通私謁。

translations.literal: After a year the imperial kin increasingly interfered in affairs and accepted private audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year imperial princes meddled in policy and accepted private petitions.

sentences.zh: 議立海軍，之洞言海軍費絀可緩立，爭之不得。

translations.literal: When a navy was debated, Zhidong said naval funds were too thin to establish it hastily and could not prevail in argument.
translations.idiomatic: Debating a new navy, Zhidong argued funds were insufficient; he lost the debate.

sentences.zh: 移疾，遂卒，年七十三，朝野震悼。

translations.literal: He reported illness and then died at seventy-three; court and country mourned.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness, died at seventy-three, and court and country mourned.

sentences.zh: 贈太保，諡文襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the posthumous title Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian with the temple name Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 之洞短身巨髯，風儀峻整。

translations.literal: Zhidong was short in stature with a great beard, his bearing stern and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Short and bearded, Zhidong carried himself with stern dignity.

sentences.zh: 蒞官所至，必有興作。

translations.literal: Wherever he took office he always launched projects.
translations.idiomatic: Every post he held saw new construction.

sentences.zh: 務宏大，不問費多寡。

translations.literal: He pursued grandeur and did not ask how much money was spent.
translations.idiomatic: He sought grandeur without counting cost.

sentences.zh: 愛才好客，名流文士爭趨之。

translations.literal: He loved talent and received guests; famous writers and scholars flocked to him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved talent and entertained guests; leading scholars gathered at his door.

sentences.zh: 任疆寄數十年，及卒，家不增一畝雲。

translations.literal: He held frontier responsibility for decades, and at death his family had not added a single mu of land.
translations.idiomatic: After decades governing provinces, his family owned not one added mu of land.

sentences.zh: 瞿鴻禨，字子玖，湖南善化人。

translations.literal: Qu Hongji, courtesy name Zijiu, was a native of Shanhua in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Hongji, courtesy name Zijiu, came from Shanhua in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 同治十年進士，授編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the tenth year of Tongzhi, he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A Tongzhi tenth-year jinshi, he became a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，大考一等，擢侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he ranked first in the palace examination and was promoted to expositor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu's first year he topped the palace examination and became Hanlin expositor.

sentences.zh: 久乃遷詹事，晉內閣學士。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was made sublector of the heir apparent and promoted to Hanlin academician of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he became sublector and then Hanlin academician of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 先後典福建、廣西鄉試，督河南、浙江、四川學政。

translations.literal: In succession he presided over the Fujian and Guangxi provincial examinations and supervised education in Henan, Zhejiang, and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He successively ran the Fujian and Guangxi provincial exams and served as educational commissioner in Henan, Zhejiang, and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 所行皆本功令，律下尤嚴。

translations.literal: What he carried out all followed official regulations, and his discipline below was especially strict.
translations.idiomatic: His administration strictly followed official regulations, with especially stern discipline.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮戰事起，我師出平壤。

translations.literal: When the Korean war arose our army marched out to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out in Korea, Chinese forces advanced on Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 鴻禨上四路進兵之策，請兼募沿海漁人蜑戶編為舟師，使敵備多力分，庶可制勝。

translations.literal: Hongji memorialized a strategy of advancing on four routes and also recruiting coastal fishermen and boat people into naval forces so the enemy would spread defenses and strength and victory might be won.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji proposed a four-route advance and recruiting coastal fishermen and boat people as naval auxiliaries to divide enemy strength.

sentences.zh: 及和議成，鴻禨方自蜀還，復奏言秦中地形險要，請豫建陪都。

translations.literal: After peace was made Hongji had just returned from Sichuan and again memorialized that Qin terrain was strategically vital and asked to prepare a secondary capital in advance.
translations.idiomatic: After peace, returning from Sichuan, he urged preparing a secondary capital in the strategic Qin region.

sentences.zh: 日本增兵遼東，鴻禨以敵情叵測，請敕劉坤一、王文韶簡練勁旅，不可專任淮軍。

translations.literal: When Japan reinforced troops in Liaodong, Hongji, because enemy intentions were hard to fathom, asked an edict that Liu Kunyi and Wang Wenshao drill crack troops and that reliance on Huai Army alone not be total.
translations.idiomatic: When Japan reinforced Liaodong, Hongji—deeming enemy intentions uncertain—ordered Liu Kunyi and Wang Wenshao to train elite troops rather than rely solely on the Huai Army.

sentences.zh: 適坤一奏劾山西將賀星明侵餉，革職，鴻禨言：「刑賞治天下之大柄，軍紀廢弛已久，宜嚴懲以儆其餘。

translations.literal: Just then Kunyi memorialized impeaching Shanxi commander He Xingming for embezzling pay and removing him from office; Hongji said: "Punishment and reward are the great handles for governing the realm; military discipline has long been lax and severe punishment should warn the rest.
translations.idiomatic: When Kunyi impeached Shanxi commander He Xingming for embezzling pay, Hongji argued: "Reward and punishment govern the realm; discipline has collapsed and severe punishment must warn others.

sentences.zh: 」又：「葉志超、龔照嶼等敗軍辱國，罪當死。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Ye Zhichao, Gong Zhaoyu, and others disgraced the army and nation and deserve death.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Ye Zhichao and Gong Zhaoyu disgraced the nation and deserve death.

sentences.zh: 和約既定，勢不能與勾，宜籍其財產，或令巨款捐贖，然後貸其一死。

translations.literal: Now that the treaty is fixed, execution is impossible; their property should be confiscated or they should ransom their lives with huge payments, then their deaths may be spared.
translations.idiomatic: With peace concluded, execution is impractical; confiscate their property or accept huge ransoms, then spare their lives.

sentences.zh: 」皆不報。

translations.literal: " None received response.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne did not respond.

sentences.zh: 旋遷禮部侍郎，出督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to vice minister of Rites and went out to supervise Jiangsu education.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became vice minister of Rites and supervised education in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 請罷武科。

translations.literal: He asked to abolish the military examination.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to abolish military examinations.

sentences.zh: 兩宮西狩，鴻禨差竣詣行在，道授左都御使，晉工部尚書，仍以西安陪都為言。

translations.literal: When the two sovereigns fled west, Hongji, having finished his assignment, went to the traveling court; en route he was made Left Censor-in-Chief and promoted to Minister of Works, again urging Xi'an as secondary capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the court fled west, Hongji joined the traveling court, was made Left Censor-in-Chief and Minister of Works en route, and again urged making Xi'an a secondary capital.

sentences.zh: 既至，命直軍機，兼充政務處大臣。

translations.literal: On arrival he was ordered to serve on the Grand Council and concurrently as minister on the Political Affairs Council.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he joined the Grand Council and the Political Affairs Council.

sentences.zh: 請以策論試士，開經濟特科，汰書吏，悉允行。

translations.literal: He asked to test scholars with policy discourse, open a special economic examination, and thin clerical staff—all approved.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed policy-discourse examinations, a special economic exam, and cutting clerks—all approved.

sentences.zh: 改總理各國事務衙門為外務部，班六部上，以鴻禨為尚書。

translations.literal: The Zongli Yamen for affairs of all nations was changed to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, ranking above the Six Ministries, with Hongji as minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Zongli Yamen became the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, ranked above the Six Ministries, with Hongji as its first minister.

sentences.zh: 時方與各國議和，鴻禨治事明敏，諳究外交，承旨擬諭，語中竅要，頗當上意焉。

translations.literal: At that time peace was being negotiated with every country; Hongji handled affairs with sharp clarity, was well versed in foreign relations, drafted edicts to instruction, his language hitting essentials, and greatly pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: During negotiations with foreign powers, Hongji handled affairs with sharp clarity, mastered diplomacy, drafted edicts that hit essentials, and pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 扈蹕回鑾，賞黃馬褂，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Escorting the return to the capital he was granted the yellow jacket and made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Escorting the court home, he received the yellow jacket and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 自新政議起，興學、通商、勸工諸政，有司多藉端巧取。

translations.literal: From the time new policies were debated, in schools, commerce, and encouraging industry many officials used pretexts to exact cleverly.
translations.idiomatic: As new policies spread, officials often used schools, commerce, and industry programs to levy extortionate fees.

sentences.zh: 鴻禨請降旨禁革苛派，任民間自辦。

translations.literal: Hongji asked an edict forbidding harsh exactions and letting the people manage affairs themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji sought an edict banning harsh levies and letting people manage reforms themselves.

sentences.zh: 又請旨以戶部正雜諸款供地方正用，宮中歲費，遵先朝定例，量入為出，不便自戶部增撥。

translations.literal: He also asked that regular and miscellaneous revenue items of the Board of Revenue supply local regular expenses, and that palace yearly costs follow ancestral fixed amounts, balancing income and outgo, not conveniently increasing Board of Revenue allocations.
translations.idiomatic: He urged funding local expenses from regular Board of Revenue accounts and limiting palace spending to ancestral quotas without extra allocations.

sentences.zh: 裁汰內務府冗員，用節糜費。

translations.literal: He cut redundant staff of the Imperial Household and thereby saved waste.
translations.idiomatic: He cut redundant Imperial Household staff to curb waste.

sentences.zh: 充中日議約全權大臣。

translations.literal: He served as plenipotentiary for the Sino-Japanese treaty.
translations.idiomatic: He served as plenipotentiary for the Sino-Japanese treaty negotiations.

sentences.zh: 是時中外咸以立憲為請，朝廷下詔豫備憲政始基，勗天下以忠君尊孔、尚公尚武尚實，用鴻禨言也。

translations.literal: At that time court and country alike asked for constitutional government; the court issued an edict preparing the foundation of constitutional government, urging the realm to loyalty to the sovereign, reverence for Confucius, and esteem for public spirit, martial spirit, and practicality—using Hongji's words.
translations.idiomatic: When China debated constitutionalism, the court issued an edict laying constitutional foundations, urging loyalty to the sovereign, reverence for Confucius, and public, martial, and practical virtues—following Hongji's counsel.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was made associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he became associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 特旨派議改官制大臣，鴻禨以樞廷事冗辭。

translations.literal: By special edict he was assigned to the commission revising the governmental system; Hongji declined because Grand Council business was too heavy.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict named him to the governmental reform commission, but he declined citing Grand Council overload.

sentences.zh: 旋命與大學士孫家鼐复核，頗有裁正焉。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to review jointly with Grand Secretary Sun Jia'nai and made many corrections.
translations.idiomatic: He was then ordered to review the plan with Grand Secretary Sun Jianai and corrected many provisions.

sentences.zh: 鴻禨持躬清刻，以儒臣驟登政地，銳於任事。

translations.literal: Hongji conducted himself with austere integrity; as a Confucian scholar suddenly elevated to power, he was keen to take on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Austere and upright, Hongji rose suddenly from scholarship to power and threw himself into affairs.

sentences.zh: 素善岑春煊，春煊入朝，留長郵傳部。

translations.literal: He had long been friendly with Cen Chunxuan; when Chunxuan entered court he was kept at the Ministry of Posts and Communications.
translations.idiomatic: He favored Cen Chunxuan, who on entering court headed the Ministry of Posts and Communications.

sentences.zh: 密疏劾慶親王奕劻，奕劻惡春煊，遂及鴻禨。

translations.literal: In a secret memorial he impeached Prince Qing Yikuang; Yikuang hated Chunxuan and therefore turned against Hongji.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly impeached Prince Qing Yikuang; Yikuang hated Cen Chunxuan and turned on Hongji as well.

sentences.zh: 會鴻禨因直言忤太后旨，侍講學士惲毓鼎劾以攬權恣縱，遂罷斥歸里。

translations.literal: When Hongji because of frank speech offended the empress dowager, Expositor Yun Yiding impeached him for grasping power and acting willfully, and he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Frank speech offended the empress dowager; Expositor Yun Yiding impeached him for grasping power, and he was dismissed to his home.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，湘變起，流寓上海，旋卒。

translations.literal: In the xinhai year Hunan revolted; he sojourned in Shanghai and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: When the 1911 revolution erupted in Hunan, he took refuge in Shanghai and soon died.

sentences.zh: 後追諡文慎。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously given the title Wenshen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with the temple name Wenshen.

sentences.zh: 論曰：德宗親政，憤於外侮，思變法自強。

translations.literal: The commentary says: When Emperor Dezong personally held government he resented foreign insult and wished to reform and strengthen himself.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: When Guangxu took personal rule, humiliated by foreign aggression, he sought reform and self-strengthening.

sentences.zh: 乃以輔導無人，戊戌黨禍，庚子匪亂，遂相繼而作。

translations.literal: Yet because there was no one to guide him, the 1898 party disaster and the 1900 Boxer turmoil followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Lacking trustworthy guidance, the 1898 purge and the 1900 Boxer catastrophe followed in turn.

sentences.zh: 太后再出垂簾，初堅復舊，繼勉圖新。

translations.literal: The empress dowager again held court behind the curtain; at first she firmly restored the old, then labored to seek the new.
translations.idiomatic: Cixi resumed regency—first bent on restoration, then pressing toward reform.

sentences.zh: 宣統改元，議行憲政。

translations.literal: When Xuantong changed the reign title, constitutional government was debated.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xuantong reign, constitutional government was debated.

sentences.zh: 政體既變，國本遂搖，而大勢不可問矣。

translations.literal: Once the political system changed, the foundation of the state shook, and the great trend could no longer be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Once institutions changed, the dynastic foundation shook and the empire's fate was beyond remedy.

sentences.zh: 榮祿屢參大變，文韶久達世務。

translations.literal: Rong Lu repeatedly took part in great changes; Wenshao long understood worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu shaped repeated crises; Wenshao long mastered practical governance.

sentences.zh: 鴻禨後起，參議立憲，終以失寵太后，不免放斥。

translations.literal: Hongji rose later, took part in debating constitutional establishment, yet in the end lost the empress dowager's favor and could not escape dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji rose later to debate constitutionalism yet lost Cixi's favor and was cast out.

sentences.zh: 唯之洞一時稱賢，而監國攝政，親貴用事，欲挽救而未能，遂以憂死。

translations.literal: Only Zhidong was for a time called worthy, but under regency the imperial kin held power; he wished to rescue the situation yet could not, and died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhidong was called the age's great minister, yet under regency princes ruled; he tried to save the state, failed, and died in grief.

sentences.zh: 人之雲亡，邦國殄瘁，尚何言哉？

translations.literal: When such men perish, the state is laid waste—what more can be said?
translations.idiomatic: When such men are gone, the state withers—what more is there to say?
